title: Tunisian rectangle wrap
subtitle: A dense rectangle in Tunisian simple stitch on an aran-weight yarn, using a long Tunisian hook
excerpt: This wrap uses Tunisian simple stitch worked on a long Tunisian crochet hook with aran-weight yarn. Each row is worked in two passes: a forward pass picks up loops across the row, and a return pass works them off. The resulting fabric is dense, warm, and knit-like in appearance. Finished size is approximately 170 cm wide by 50 cm deep. A long Tunisian hook (or extension cable hook) is required.
heroPrompt: A rectangular Tunisian crochet wrap in warm ochre aran-weight yarn folded over the arm of a linen sofa, showing the knit-like vertical rib texture of Tunisian simple stitch, photographed in soft light.

glossaryTerms.definition: The foundational Tunisian stitch. Insert hook under the vertical bar of the stitch from the previous row, yarn over and pull up a loop (keeping all loops on hook for the forward pass). Then work the return pass by yarning over and pulling through loops in pairs across the hook from right to left.
The first half of a Tunisian row, in which you insert the hook into each stitch and pull up a loop, holding all loops on the hook without working them off.
The second half of a Tunisian row, in which you work off the loops accumulated in the forward pass by yarning over and pulling through two loops at a time from right to left, until one loop remains.

content.text: Tunisian crochet is worked with a long hook that holds all the live loops of a row at once. This wrap uses Tunisian simple stitch throughout, producing a dense, knit-like fabric with a clear vertical rib on the right side. Each row of the pattern is two passes: the forward pass picks up one loop per stitch across the row without working them off, and the return pass works through all those loops from right to left. A dedicated long Tunisian hook (at least 50 cm, or a standard hook with an extension cable) is needed to hold 80 or more live loops.
The
Tunisian simple stitch (Tss)
picks up loops through the vertical bars of the previous row on the
forward pass
, and the
return pass
works them off. Unlike standard crochet, you do not turn the work between passes: both passes travel in the same direction across the same face of the fabric.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 500 g aran-weight yarn. A 5.5 mm Tunisian crochet hook at least 50 cm long, or a standard 5.5 mm hook fitted with a flexible extension cable. Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Blocking mat and pins. Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge

16 Tss sts x 14 rows = 10 x 10 cm in aran-weight yarn with a 5.5 mm Tunisian hook, measured after blocking. Each 'row' here counts as one forward pass plus one return pass. Tunisian fabric curls before blocking; swatch and block the swatch before measuring.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared, used for foundation chain.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared, used for cast-off.
Tunisian simple stitch (Tss): worked in two passes as described above.
Pattern

The wrap is worked flat from one short end to the other. The foundation chain is the 50 cm depth; the rows build the 170 cm width. You do not turn the work at the end of each row in Tunisian crochet: the fabric is always facing you on the right side.
Foundation chain
Ch 81. (This gives 80 working stitches across the 50 cm depth.)
Foundation row (forward pass)
Insert hook into 2nd ch from hook, yarn over, pull up loop (keep on hook). *Insert hook into next ch, yarn over, pull up loop*; repeat from * to * to end. Do not turn. (81 loops on hook)
Foundation row (return pass)
Yarn over, pull through 1 loop. *Yarn over, pull through 2 loops*; repeat from * to * to end until 1 loop remains on hook. (80 sts)
Row 1 (forward pass)

Skip first vertical bar (this is the selvedge edge). *Insert hook under next vertical bar from front to back, yarn over, pull up loop (keep on hook)*; repeat from * to * across all 79 remaining vertical bars. Insert hook under both loops of the last stitch at the far edge, yarn over, pull up loop. Do not turn. (81 loops on hook)
Row 1 (return pass)
Yarn over, pull through 1 loop. *Yarn over, pull through 2 loops*; repeat from * to * to end until 1 loop remains on hook. (80 sts)
Continue to approximately row 238
Repeat row 1 (forward pass + return pass) until the piece measures 170 cm from the foundation chain edge, approximately 238 rows. The stitch count remains 80 sts throughout.
Cast off
Work a slip-stitch cast-off row: *insert hook under next vertical bar, yarn over, pull through bar and loop on hook (1 sl st made)*; repeat from * to * across all stitches. Fasten off.
Finishing

Fasten off and weave in both ends through the back of several Tss stitches. Tunisian fabric curls at the edges before blocking. Wet-block by soaking thoroughly, pressing out excess water, and pinning flat to 170 x 50 cm on a blocking mat. The fabric flattens completely once blocked and dry.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild wool wash. Do not tumble-dry. Lay flat to dry. Blocking after each wash keeps the fabric flat.
What to try next

Tunisian full stitch (Tfs) uses the same two-pass structure but inserts through the space between vertical bars rather than the bar itself, giving a more open, mesh-like fabric. Colour-change stripes are straightforward in Tunisian: change yarn at the start of a return pass. A narrow standard dc border worked around all four edges after blocking tidies the curl-prone selvedges.
